code: $comment = new DOMComment("This is the first comment.");
note: A DOMComment object is created and then reinitialized, exercising the constructor-on-existing-object path.
The same wrapper is constructed again, which causes the implementation to fetch and free any prior node stored in the object.
A fresh libxml comment node is allocated from attacker-controlled text.
The wrapper's previous node pointer is read before replacement.
The previous node is freed here; the vulnerability hypothesis is that the constructor-on-existing-object path can free stale or uninitialized memory when the wrapper state is inconsistent.
The wrapper is updated after the free, so the free is the relevant sink for the crash hypothesis.
